assessments.reasoning: Sections 5.9 and 5.10 distinguish equal-size vector component multiplication from the dimension-matched matrix/vector product. The right-hand vector is a column. The manual's component equations use the stored matrix columns in the latter case.

challenge.method: Recompute a nonsymmetric mat3 times vec3 using the component equations. Compare operand-reversed multiplication and a separate vec3 times vec3 calculation. Check the cited matrix component-wise built-in and dimension rule.
challenge.results: Using matrix columns (1,2,3), (4,5,6), (7,8,9) and vector (2,3,5) gives column result (49,59,69), distinct from the left-vector result (23,53,83). Pairing (7,11,13) with (2,3,5) by vector multiplication gives (14,33,65). The separate function matrixCompMult is not an alternative meaning of these operator uses.

limitations: Both operands have the claimed concrete floating-point types and the dimensions conform. The finite example challenges orientation, without drawing conclusions about mixed types, precision, or a particular implementation.
